name: Proton Unlimited
tagline: Encrypted email, calendar, VPN, password manager, and cloud storage

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Proton Free
tiers.limits: 1 user; 1 email address; 1 GB storage initially, expandable to 5 GB by completing account actions; limited VPN and Pass

tiers.name: Proton Unlimited
tiers.limits: 1 user; 500 GB storage; 15 email addresses; 3 custom domains; 10 VPN connections; up to 50 password vaults
tiers.notes: $119.88 billed annually at the published annual-equivalent rate.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 user; 1 email address; 1 GB initial storage (up to 5 GB after account actions); limited VPN and password-manager access
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual Unlimited is $9.99/month equivalent
pricing.hiddenCosts: Taxes can be added; storage, addresses and users above the included personal limits require a different Proton plan, and discounted acquisition offers can renew at the then-current standard rate

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Proton Unlimited's durable value is security, infrastructure, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for privacy suite; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness
global network or redundant storage infrastructure
whyPeopleStillPay: Proton Unlimited: Security subscriptions buy professional operations, audits, response capacity, redundancy, and accountability when something goes wrong.
ongoingBurden: Own threat modelling, key management, patching, backups, restore tests, incident response, privacy requests, and dependency security.

priorArt.name: Nextcloud
priorArt.desc: Open-source file sync, sharing, and collaboration server.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Nextcloud Files
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Drive and calendar are credible; encrypted mail, consumer VPN, and a password manager are separate projects.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Proton Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Mail, calendar, drive, passwords, and VPN are free; the storage and VPN limits are the whole reason Unlimited exists.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Syncthing
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A superb file-sync engine replacing roughly one-fifth of the suite.

notes: Credibility row: Proton Unlimited survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Proton Unlimited; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Go 1.24 + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local diagnostic or backup companion for privacy suite; do not claim to replace audited security, identity, VPN, or cloud-storage infrastructure.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: calendar-provider edge cases and timezone correctness; audited cryptography and incident response; global network or redundant storage infrastructure.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
